Report Verbs with Impersonal Passive Constructions
You can use the structure: It + passive report verb + finite clause (a clause which can stand alone) to report information.

For example:
It is thought that the Pyramids took 25 years to build.

This pattern is often used in formal reports, news reports and academic writing.

You can use that structure with the following verbs:
It is believed that some team roles may not be required.
It is supposed that including a Plant on the team would be counterproductive.
It is shown that they may want to come up with something new altogether.
It is recommended that teams pay careful attention to how many of each role are on the team.
It is understood that there are times when social roles may not be as necessary as thinking and action roles.

images.text: Different teams have different purposes, so it is believed that some team roles may not be required when setting one up. The absence of a particular role is not always a potential problem. If a team has specific parameters to work within for the creation of a new ad campaign, it is supposed that including a Plant on the team would be counterproductive, in that they may want to come up with something new altogether and not work within the constraints.

Since there may be times in a project where a missing role becomes necessary, it is worth thinking about how to fill that gap. Can someone currently on the team take on the role or should additional staff be brought in to provide a particular contribution?

There may be overlaps or gaps in team roles because most people will fit into more than one role. It is recommended that teams pay careful attention to how many people in each role are on the team. A lot of Plants on a team may result in too many ideas competing for attention and a large number of Shapers can cause aggressive behavior within the group.

Too many Specialists may cause territorial behavior, and Completer Finishers may step on each other's toes, competing for the final “sign‐off” on the work. All team roles can be grouped into thinking, social, and action-oriented. As the purpose of each team will be different, the three areas will be represented in different numbers on each team. It is understood that there are times when social roles may not be as necessary as thinking and action roles, and vice versa. It can be concluded there is no right or wrong way to form a team.
